messages:
Emily (Support): FYI customer NexaHealth reported a p95 jump on hosted inference after last night's catalog rollout, started ~00:10 UTC. Link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/abcd/nexa-p95 :eyes:
Mina (PM): Can you paste the exact metric and timeframe? Is this across all models or a specific route?
Emily (Support): p95 for /v1/chat/completions increased from ~180ms -> ~650ms between 00:08-00:15. Traffic volume steady. Affected route: customer-nexa-chat (model routing enabled).
Ben (Eng lead): Do we have any recent routing changes? Last deploy note showed we enabled model variants fallback for that route yesterday. Might be routing to a heavier quantized variant.
obs-bot: Alert: route "customer-nexa-chat" 00:08 UTC — p95 650ms, error rate 0.2% — topology change detected.
Josh (Oncall): Pulling logs. Quick grep shows a spike in requests hitting redwood-v2-large-heimdall variant with cold KV cache misses. Sample log:
```
2026-03-19T00:09:23Z req=xyz route=customer-nexa-chat target=redwood-v2-large-heimdall cache_status=miss latency_ms=612
2026-03-19T00:09:24Z req=ab2 route=customer-nexa-chat target=redwood-v2-large-heimdall cache_status=miss latency_ms=640
```
Josh (Oncall): So two signals: routing selected a heavier variant, and KV cache miss pattern causing startup token overhead.
Kara (Sales): Nexa is on our hosted plan (paid). They flagged SLA risk — they asked for priority escalation if this affects more than 5% of requests.
Mina (PM): Short term triage items: 1) Pin their route to redwood-v2-medium (owner: Ben) 2) Rollback variant fallback that was deployed (owner: EngInfra) 3) Provide Nexa a mitigation ETA and temporary config (owner: Emily/Kara). Long term: consider route-level "preferred variants" to avoid auto-fallbacks for paid customers — needs prioritization.
Ben (Eng lead): I can pin route and patch routing policy within 30 min. Need a quick feature check: will pinning bypass autoscaling/burst? Josh, can you confirm no further capacity side-effects?
Josh (Oncall): Pin is safe — it's just routing policy. Autoscaler still scales the target pool. But if we pin to a smaller variant we must ensure the dedicated pool has capacity; for hosted we'll rely on general pool.
Emily (Support): I'll update Nexa: "We see a routing to a heavier variant + cache effects. Temporary fix: pin to redwood-v2-medium while we investigate. ETA 30-60m."
Mina (PM): Acceptance criteria for customer-facing fix: reproducer confirmed internally, pin applied, p95 < 250ms for 30m, and customer notified. For roadmap/ops ask: scope doc for "customer pinning" feature — include UX, API, rollout gating, and SLA semantics.
Kara (Sales): Can we offer SLA credit now or after we validate mitigation? Customer wants reassurance.
Mina (PM): Hold off on credit until we have root cause; offer status updates and a prioritized mitigation timeline.
Ben (Eng lead): I'll create a short RFC for the pinning feature if we think it needs product work to expose safely. For now I'll execute the pin.
Josh (Oncall): After pin we should run a simulated traffic replay against the target variant to confirm KV warmup behavior. I'll take that.
Emily (Support): Nexa message queued. I'll post a status update once pin is applied.
Mina (PM): Next steps: Ben apply pin (owner), Josh run replay and validate latency (owner), Emily notify customer (owner), Mina draft scope doc for product prioritization (owner). Can we sync in 1h in #product-ops? :white_check_mark:
Ben (Eng lead): On it.
Kara (Sales): Thanks team. I'll brief the customer after Emily's update. :pray:
